summary:
Repaired the broken relative Markdown links in docs/intent/PROJECT_GOALS.md. My own count agrees with the Manager's exactly: 7 link occurrences across 5 distinct targets, so no count difference is recorded. Every relative link was resolved by me against the repository with `git ls-files` plus a filesystem existence test, without trusting the supplied list. Each of the 5 old targets was missing and each of the 5 new targets was confirmed to exist before it was written:
- ../specs/STRATEGY_ECONOMICS.md -> ../spec/strategy/STRATEGY_ECONOMICS.md (lines 212 and 563)
- ../specs/OPERATOR_CONTROL.md -> ../spec/operations/OPERATOR_CONTROL.md (lines 370 and 565)
- ./ASSET_ADMISSION.md -> ../spec/product/ASSET_ADMISSION.md (line 384)
- ./WEB_CONSOLE.md -> ../spec/product/WEB_CONSOLE.md (line 567)
- ./TRACEABILITY.md -> ../implement/TRACEABILITY.md (line 568)
Exactly one file changed, 7 insertions and 7 deletions, all of them link targets. A re-resolution pass over the edited file reports 0 broken relative links. A repo-wide scan of every tracked *.md file for relative links that do not resolve reports 0 broken links outside this file. Per the direction, section 10's two prose file names (docs/spec/product/USE_CASES.md, docs/intent/SUCCESS_CRITERIA.md) were left byte-identical: they remain plain backticked prose, were not turned into links, and no such file was created. No task was created and no workflow state changed; `python3 -m tools.workflow validate` returns {"status": "OK"} (run as investigation only, not as acceptance evidence).
rationale: A goal document is the first artifact a reader opens, and a link that points nowhere is read as evidence that the referenced document was never written rather than as a typo. The change is confined to the smallest edit that removes that false signal: five link targets, with the surrounding sentences, the requirement set and the document structure untouched. The two failure modes were left distinct on purpose. The ../specs/ links were broken by a directory rename followed by a reorganisation into subdirectories, so the repair follows the file into docs/spec/<area>/; the ./ASSET_ADMISSION.md, ./WEB_CONSOLE.md and ./TRACEABILITY.md links were broken because the files moved out of docs/intent/ altogether, into docs/spec/product/ and docs/implement/. In section 10 the two missing names are prose declarations of documents to be written later, which is a different claim from a link that fails, so repairing a link there would have overwritten an intentional statement of future work. The requested outcome is a repair, not an editorial pass, so nothing else was touched, including the unchanged `最后更新` header and todo/config.yaml. The one file changed sits under docs/intent/, which is inside the PROPHET layer's scope, and the change is a modification rather than a deletion or a task-contract edit, so it satisfies the two enforced bounds on this layer.
unresolved_questions: docs/intent/PROJECT_GOALS.md is the binding V1 goal and acceptance baseline, yet its content has now changed while `intent_revision` in todo/config.yaml remains `v1-2026-09-19-research-universe-numeraire`. The Owner direction explicitly forbade touching todo/config.yaml, and the PROPHET layer permits the two revisions to differ without requiring it, so I left it alone; nothing else in the repository pins that value. Open question: should a link-only repair to a goal document bump `intent_revision`, so that a reader binding to a revision can tell that the text with that revision changed? No action was taken either way.

Section 10 declares two documents that do not exist and that no other artifact in the repository owns: `docs/spec/product/USE_CASES.md` and `docs/intent/SUCCESS_CRITERIA.md`. A search of todo/config.yaml, todo/phases/ and all of docs/ finds these names only in these two sentences, so no task is scheduled to write either one. This direction told me not to create them, not to link them and not to remove the sentences, which I obeyed, and it did not ask for a task. Open question: does the Owner want a task created for these two documents, or are the sentences meant to stay as unnamed future work?

No gate in this repository could have caught the defect this amendment repairs. tests/test_workflow_contracts.py::test_binding_documents_use_the_new_layer_paths asserts only that the literal substrings `docs/specs/`, `docs/product/` and similar never appear in the checked roots, but the stale links here were written as `../specs/...` and `./ASSET_ADMISSION.md`, neither of which contains a forbidden prefix. A search for any link-checking tooling (linkcheck, link_check, check_links) finds none. So this class of breakage is invisible to CI, and a future rename can reintroduce it. Closing that gap means editing tests/, which is in no layer's scope and changes only by an explicit bootstrap act; I did not touch it and am raising it rather than acting on it.

The header of docs/intent/PROJECT_GOALS.md reads `最后更新：2026-09-16`, but `git log` shows the file was last changed on 2026-09-19 by c7a788d. The date was already stale before this amendment and is not something this amendment introduced. The direction said to change nothing but the link targets, so I did not update it; recording it only because it was found.
